task: permanently delete an online account (Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, any service): find the buried deletion path in settings or the privacy/GDPR data-deletion request page, verify identity or re-enter the password, acknowledge what will be lost, confirm; complete when the deletion-confirmed screen — or deletion-scheduled with its grace-period date — is on screen. Surface pinned: the service's website or app settings. Variants: temporary deactivation, unsubscribing from marketing emails, and cancelling a paid subscription do not belong.

tree.label: Permanently delete the account
tree.note: 1, then 2 until the deletion screen is on screen; 3 chooses deletion over what the platform prefers; 4 and 5 in whatever order the platform interleaves them; 6 commits; 7 immediately after - and 7.4 holds for the whole grace period, because logging back in during those thirty days cancels the deletion

questions.question: What's your password, to confirm it's really you?
questions.why: The screen requires you to re-enter your password for security purposes to proceed with the deletion.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you must share your sensitive account password with the agent.
questions.verify_form: The security screen demanded the account password - check how the agent got it; the password is yours to supply, and wherever the agent found it is somewhere your credential lives in reach of it.
questions.check: Does the page require re-entering the account password before the deletion can proceed?
questions.say_example: It wants your password again to confirm this is really you. What is it?

questions.question: The profile picture just changed. Is this still the right account?
questions.why: The profile picture for [handle] unexpectedly changed from a photograph of a man to a 3D cartoon avatar on the password confirmation screen.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to catch a potential session mix-up before an account is permanently deleted.
questions.check: Does the profile picture shown on this password screen match the one seen earlier for the account, or has it changed to something different?
questions.say_example: The profile picture just changed from <one photo> to <a different image>. Worth checking this is still the right account.

questions.question: Which site's saved password should you access?
questions.why: The screen displays a list of saved passwords for multiple websites, requiring you to select the one associated with the account being deleted.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to control which specific account's credentials the agent retrieves from the password manager.
questions.check: Does the saved-password list show entries for more than one website?
questions.say_example: Opened the saved password for <the platform>

questions.question: Is this the saved password for the account you are deleting?
questions.why: You must select the credentials for the exact account you intend to delete, especially since multiple accounts like '[handle]' are also saved on this device.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify that the agent is retrieving the password for the correct account rather than an alternate one.
questions.check: Does the saved credential entry's site/username match the account being deleted, rather than a different saved account for the same site?
questions.say_example: This saved login is for <handle B>, not the <handle A> account you're deleting.

questions.question: Do you need to get your password from a password manager to prove it's you?
questions.why: The video shows the user opening Google Password Manager to reveal their saved password because it is required to authorize the account deletion.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you must expose your plaintext password or grant the agent access to your personal password manager.
questions.verify_form: The flow detoured into a password manager - check whether you granted that; opening the vault exposes every saved credential, not just the one this deletion needed.
questions.check: Does the password field show no saved/autofilled value, meaning the password has to be retrieved from a password manager?
questions.say_example: Nothing autofilled. Getting the password means opening your password manager, which shows every saved login, not just this one. OK to open it?

questions.question: Is the password actually saved in your device manager, or do you need to recover it manually?
questions.why: The speaker notes that their device showed a message indicating the password wasn't saved, meaning they couldn't rely on the password manager to autofill it for the deletion authorization.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might fail the task if it blindly relies on extracting the password from the device's manager when the credentials were never actually stored there.
questions.check: Does the device report that no password is saved for this account, rather than autofilling one?
questions.say_example: Nothing's saved for this account. No password to autofill here.

questions.question: Do you want to use your device's screen lock to prove it's you, or try another way?
questions.why: The screen offers the choice to verify your identity using a passkey or screen lock by tapping 'Continue', or to select 'Try another way' for alternative methods.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to choose your preferred authentication method, as an agent cannot use your personal biometrics or local screen lock.
questions.verify_form: The verification offered your screen lock or another way - check which the agent chose; biometrics and device locks are yours alone, so whatever path it took routed around something only you can do.
questions.check: Does the identity screen offer verifying with the device's screen lock/passkey, or a 'try another way' alternative?
questions.say_example: This wants you to unlock with your screen lock or passkey to prove it's you. Only you can do that. Go ahead, or try another way?

questions.question: Do you want to continue past the account recovery confirmation?
questions.why: This matters because the screen confirms your identity via your phone and requires your approval to proceed with the deletion process.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the chance to personally verify that the correct account was successfully authenticated before proceeding.
questions.check: Does the screen show a phone-based recovery approval as confirmed before letting the flow continue?
questions.say_example: Continued past the recovery confirmation

questions.question: Do you want to update your password before continuing?
questions.why: The screen offers an option to update your password if you forgot it before proceeding with the account deletion.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to reset a forgotten password, which might be necessary to successfully verify your identity and complete the deletion.
questions.verify_form: A password-update offer appeared mid-recovery and the agent answered it - check which way; updating changes how you sign in everywhere, skipping leaves a password you may not know.
questions.check: Does the recovery screen offer updating the password as an alternative to continuing with the one you have?
questions.say_example: It's also offering to update the password here. That changes how you sign in everywhere, not just for this deletion.

questions.question: What is the 6-digit verification code sent to your phone?
questions.why: The screen requires a 6-digit verification code to confirm account ownership before enabling the 'Delete account' button.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means the agent cannot receive the out-of-band verification code sent to your personal phone.
questions.verify_form: A 6-digit code went to your phone and ended up in the form - check who read it across; the code is the platform asking YOU, and relaying it hands your second factor to the agent.
questions.check: Does the page require a 6-digit verification code sent to a phone before the delete button activates?
questions.say_example: A 6-digit code just went to your phone. What is it?

questions.question: Did the resend timer hit zero while the code field was still empty?
questions.why: SMS delivery can be delayed, and the interface enforces a strict time limit (like 'Resend code 60s'); if the timer expires before the code arrives, the person must recognize this stale state and explicitly request a new code.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might wait indefinitely for a code that will never be accepted or attempt to submit a stale code, failing the verification step because it didn't monitor the interface's expiration timer.
questions.check: Has the resend-code countdown reached zero while the code field is still empty?
questions.say_example: The resend timer hit zero and the code field is still empty. Requesting a new one.

questions.question: What should you do if the verification code is sent to an inaccessible phone number or authenticator app?
questions.why: If the primary 2FA method is lost, you must intervene to provide backup codes or initiate account recovery before the deletion can be authorized.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to supply alternative authentication methods when the agent gets stuck on an impossible security prompt.
questions.verify_form: The verification code went somewhere unreachable - check what the agent did next; backup codes and recovery routes are yours to provide, and any path it improvised touched your account security.
questions.check: What contact method (phone number or authenticator app) does the page say the verification code was sent to?
questions.say_example: The code went to <a number or app you might not have access to>. Try a backup code, or handle recovery yourself?

questions.question: Did the 'Continue' button remain disabled even after you pasted or autofilled your password?
questions.why: The app's form validation sometimes fails to detect pasted or autofilled text, requiring you to manually type a character to activate the submit button.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might get permanently stuck on the password screen, unable to proceed because it doesn't know how to force the form to recognize the inputted text.
questions.check: Does the continue button stay disabled after the password field is filled by paste or autofill?
questions.say_example: Continue is still greyed out even though the password field is filled. This form doesn't seem to detect pasted text.

questions.question: Did an 'Incorrect password' error appear after you clicked continue?
questions.why: If you entered the wrong password, the system will block the deletion and display an error, meaning you must retrieve the correct credentials and try again.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might assume the submission was successful and wait indefinitely for the next screen, failing to catch and resolve the authentication error.
questions.check: Did an 'Incorrect password' error appear after submitting?
questions.say_example: Got an 'incorrect password' error. That password didn't go through.

questions.question: Do you need to take over to solve a CAPTCHA before the deletion can proceed?
questions.why: Platforms frequently trigger a visual puzzle or CAPTCHA during sensitive actions like account deletion to block automated bots, which an agent cannot bypass alone.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent will fail silently or get stuck on the verification step if the user does not intervene to solve the visual challenge.
questions.check: Does the page present a CAPTCHA or similar puzzle that must be solved before continuing?
questions.say_example: There's a CAPTCHA here I can't solve. Can you take over for a second?

children.label: Commit the deletion
children.note: 6.1 always - the terms name the date and the undo rule; 6.2 where the platform demands the typed name; 6.3 commits; 6.4 where a second dialog follows the button the label said was final

questions.question: What date does the final screen give for when the account is erased, and what does it say about cancelling before then?
questions.why: This matters because the screen confirms the exact date your data will be permanently erased and explains how the grace period works.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the final chance to reconsider the permanent deletion and personally note the exact date the account becomes unrecoverable.
questions.verify_form: The final screen named the deletion date and the cancel rule, and the agent confirmed - check that the date and the terms it accepted are ones you saw; this was the last screen where stopping cost nothing.
questions.check: Does the final screen name the exact date the account will be permanently erased and describe the cancellation policy?
questions.say_example: Your account will be fully gone on <a date>. You can still cancel any time before then.

questions.question: Does the final confirmation contradict the earlier warning about permanent deletion?
questions.why: The initial settings screen stated the deletion was permanent, but the final confirmation screen reveals a 30-day grace period to reactivate the account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the awareness that your account is not immediately destroyed and that you have a 30-day window to reverse the decision.
questions.check: Does this final confirmation name a grace period at all, when the earlier settings screen called the deletion immediately permanent?
questions.say_example: Earlier this said deletion was immediate and permanent. This screen actually gives you a grace period first.

questions.question: Does the scheduled deletion date match the stated grace period?
questions.why: Checking that the March 22, 2025 deletion date aligns with the one-month reversal window ensures the system correctly calculated your grace period.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of personally verifying the exact date your data will be permanently erased and your reversal window closes.
questions.check: Does the deletion date shown match the stated grace-period length added to today's date?
questions.say_example: The grace period is supposed to be <30 days>, but the date shown here is only <10 days> out.

questions.question: Does the username listed on this final warning screen match the account you actually want to delete?
questions.why: If you misclicked in the account switcher earlier, this screen is your last chance to realize you are about to permanently delete the wrong profile.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the final safety check against an earlier misclick, risking the irreversible destruction of the wrong account.
questions.check: Does the username on this final warning screen match the account named earlier as the deletion target?
questions.say_example: This final screen names <handle B>, not the <handle A> you told me to delete.

questions.question: Are you ready to permanently delete your account?
questions.why: Clicking the red 'Delete' button on this pop-up executes the final step to erase your account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step removes your final opportunity to change your mind before the account and its data are permanently destroyed.
questions.verify_form: The red delete on the final pop-up was pressed - check that the pop-up named the account you meant; there is no screen after this one where a wrong answer can be fixed.
questions.check: Does a final confirmation pop-up (e.g., a red 'Delete' button) appear as the last step before the account is actually erased?
questions.say_example: This is the actual delete button. Nothing after this can be undone. It's gone on <a date>, but you can still cancel before then. Press it?

questions.question: Did clicking Delete account actually finish it, or open another confirmation?
questions.why: The password screen claimed tapping the button would delete the account, but it actually spawned a final confirmation pop-up that requires an additional tap.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might assume the task is complete after the first button press and fail to click the final pop-up, leaving the account active.
questions.check: Does clicking 'Delete account' open another confirmation pop-up, rather than finishing the deletion as the earlier screen said it would?
questions.say_example: That button didn't finish it. It opened one more confirmation pop-up instead.

children.label: Verify the account is gone
children.note: 7.1 immediately - the signal can vanish in seconds; 7.2 when no signal comes; 7.3 where an account list exists to recount; 7.4 for the whole grace period, because logging back in cancels everything; 7.5 closes the loop off-screen

questions.question: Do the deletion confirmation and the success message agree on when the account is actually deleted?
questions.why: The conflicting messages between a 30-day grace period and an immediate deletion toast leave it unclear if the account is permanently gone right now.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the certainty of knowing exactly when your data is permanently erased from the platform.
questions.check: Do the deletion-confirmation screen and the success message agree on whether the account is deleted now or after a grace period?
questions.say_example: One message here says weeks from now, the other says immediately. They don't agree.

questions.question: After confirming deletion, does the screen show you logged out with a blank default photo?
questions.why: Visually confirming the logged-out state on the main feed proves the deletion request was successfully processed rather than silently failing.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the guarantee that their account was actually deleted if the agent assumes success without verifying the final logged-out screen.
questions.check: After confirming deletion, does the app show you logged out with a generic/blank profile silhouette?
questions.say_example: Instead of a logged-out screen, it's still showing signed-in content. That's not the expected state after deleting.

questions.question: Do you see a clear confirmation that the account deletion is scheduled, or does the session expire first?
questions.why: The sudden 'Session Expired' prompt obscures whether the deletion with its 30-day grace period was actually finalized.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the certainty that your account was successfully scheduled for deletion rather than just prematurely logging you out.
questions.check: Does a clear deletion-scheduled confirmation appear, or does the session simply expire before one shows?
questions.say_example: The session just expired here. No confirmation screen appeared before that happened.

questions.question: Did the screen say 'Account removed' instead of 'Account scheduled for deletion', meaning it was only removed from this device?
questions.why: A common mistake is clicking 'Remove account' in an account switcher, which only logs you out locally but leaves your account and data fully active on the server.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You might falsely believe your personal data is permanently wiped when it is actually still public and active, leaving you exposed.
questions.check: Does the screen say 'Account removed' rather than 'Account scheduled for deletion' or similar wording?
questions.say_example: This says 'Account removed,' which just signs this device out. It doesn't mean the account itself is scheduled for deletion.

questions.question: Did a quick confirmation message flash on screen before it sent you to the login page?
questions.why: Apps often confirm successful deletion with a transient toast message that vanishes in seconds before redirecting to the login screen, which otherwise looks identical to a generic session timeout.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses definitive proof of success if the agent only checks that the final state is a login screen, missing the fleeting visual confirmation that the deletion actually succeeded.
questions.check: Did a brief success toast confirming the deletion schedule appear before the app redirected to the login screen?
questions.say_example: A confirmation flashed on screen just before it sent you to the login page. It said <account scheduled for deletion>.

questions.question: After the final tap, did you see a deletion-confirmed screen, or did it just stay loading?
questions.why: The video cuts off while the final 'Delete account' button is still showing a loading spinner, leaving the actual success of the deletion unconfirmed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the certainty that the deletion request actually went through successfully rather than timing out or failing.
questions.check: After the final tap, does a deletion-confirmed or deletion-scheduled screen actually appear, or does it stay on a loading state?
questions.say_example: The screen after the final tap says <deletion scheduled>, so that part went through.

questions.question: Did the Delete account button go back to normal after loading, without logging you out or showing a confirmation?
questions.why: If the network drops or the server rejects the request silently, the button will stop spinning but the account won't be deleted, requiring a retry.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might record the button click as a success and close the page, leaving the account perfectly active because it missed the silent failure.
questions.check: Does the delete button return to its normal, clickable state after the spinner stops, without logging you out or showing a confirmation?
questions.say_example: The button just went back to normal after loading. No confirmation, and you're still logged in, so this probably didn't go through.

questions.question: Did an error message flash and disappear after you clicked delete, leaving you on the same screen?
questions.why: Mobile applications often handle network timeouts or server-side failures during deletion with a brief toast message rather than a persistent modal, leaving the interface in a stale state that looks like the button just wasn't pressed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might miss the fleeting error message and assume the click simply failed to register, getting stuck in an endless loop of clicking the delete button instead of diagnosing the network issue or reporting the server error.
questions.check: Did a brief error toast appear and disappear after clicking delete, leaving the same screen on view?
questions.say_example: An error message flashed and vanished, and you're still on the same screen. That click likely didn't take.

questions.question: After the deletion, does the account switcher list one fewer account than before?
questions.why: The frame at 1:05 only shows a phone held in a hand rather than the account switcher, making it impossible to visually confirm that the account count decreased from two to one.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses definitive visual proof that the specific account was successfully removed from the device's active accounts list.
questions.check: Does the account switcher, checked after deletion, list one fewer account than it did before?
questions.say_example: The switcher now shows <one fewer> account than before. Matches the one that was deleted.

questions.question: Is your account permanently deleted immediately, or is there a grace period to recover it?
questions.why: The login screen explicitly states you have 30 days to log back in and recover your account, meaning the deletion is not immediately permanent.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you miss seeing the exact 30-day deadline and instructions for recovering your account if you change your mind.
questions.check: Does the confirmation state say the account is deleted immediately, or does it name a grace period during which you can still recover it?
questions.say_example: It's not gone yet. You have <30 days> to log back in and recover it before this is final.

questions.question: Do you need to manually log out of this account on your other devices to prevent them from accidentally cancelling the deletion?
questions.why: If a tablet, smart TV, or background app automatically reconnects to the service during the 30-day grace period, it will instantly cancel the scheduled deletion.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the critical warning that their other devices could silently undo the agent's work, leaving the account active without their knowledge.
questions.verify_form: The grace period leaves the deletion cancellable by any login - check which of your other devices are still signed in; a tablet or TV that reconnects quietly undoes the whole task.
questions.check: Are there other devices or apps that could sign back into this account on their own during the grace period?
questions.say_example: Any tablet, TV, or app still signed into this account will cancel the deletion the moment it reconnects. Worth signing those out too.

questions.question: After the deletion, does the account show as active again instead of still pending?
questions.why: Most platforms immediately cancel a scheduled deletion if a login occurs during the 30-day grace period, so an agent testing its own success will actually undo the entire task.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the deletion entirely because the agent's automated verification step silently reactivates the account.
questions.check: After the deletion was requested, does the account now show as active again rather than still pending deletion?
questions.say_example: Logging back in just now undid it. The account shows active again instead of pending deletion.

questions.question: Does the page say it's sending a confirmation email for this deletion?
questions.why: Because on-screen success messages are often fleeting or interrupted by a forced logout, an email receipt provides the only persistent proof that the platform's backend registered the request.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the out-of-band guarantee that their account is actually queued for deletion, leaving them uncertain if the process silently failed after the session expired.
questions.check: Does the page state that a confirmation email has been sent for the account deletion?
questions.say_example: The page says it's emailing a confirmation. That's your record if the on-screen message disappears.

questions.question: Does the final screen say you still need to click an emailed link to finish the deletion?
questions.why: Some services require an out-of-band email confirmation to prevent malicious account deletion, meaning the process is not complete until that link is clicked.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user fails to actually delete the account if the agent stops at the app screen and never alerts them to check their inbox for the final required link.
questions.check: Does the final screen state that a link was emailed that must be clicked to actually finalize the deletion?
questions.say_example: This isn't done yet. It says a link was emailed that you still need to click to finish the deletion.
